title: Chapter 10: Mirror Mirror
html:
Phew. I scared myself for nothing.Gao Ru Xue’s breathing came unevenly, her heart racing. It had been a long time since she had lost her composure like this.

The eerie music continued playing. In the dim light, she saw the pupils of her reflection contract. Behind her reflected image, the mosquito netting began to open on its own. The face of a paper mannequin emerged from behind it, smiling directly at her through the mirror.

“Who’s there?!” Extreme fear could turn quickly into anger. Gao Ru Xue whirled around, but there was nothing behind her. She rushed to the bed and yanked at the mosquito netting to see what it concealed. The layers were more complicated than she expected, however, and instead of pulling them aside, she tangled herself in them.

Just then, she heard footsteps from inside the room.

I’m not moving, so whose footsteps are those?He San’s disappearance, combined with the effect of Black Friday, had worn down Gao Ru Xue’s psychological defenses. The unfamiliar footsteps became the final blow.

Her legs weakened until she could barely move. Fear tore at her rational mind like an animal straining against a cage. Gao Ru Xue tugged desperately at the netting, but the more she struggled, the more tangled she became. The footsteps drew steadily closer.

Impossible! The room is tiny. If someone were coming toward me, I’d be able to see them!Her thoughts were in chaos. Even the simplest decorations in the room now sent chills down her spine.

The white lantern outside the window swayed in the wind, dimming the room. Gao Ru Xue’s reflection blurred in the bronze mirror. Her eyes widened when she realized that the figure staring back at her was no longer herself, but a strange woman in a wedding dress.

The woman possessed an eerie, almost unreal beauty—captivating and unsettling at the same time, like an exquisite work of art uncovered after years in darkness.

Staring at the woman in the mirror, Gao Ru Xue’s lips trembled. For the first time, fear showed openly on her face.

Her forensic training had made her familiar with the appearance of the dead, and the woman in the mirror gave her the unmistakable impression of a corpse.

There’s a real corpse in this Haunted House!The thought sent a wave of fear through her. Gao Ru Xue tried to get away from the bronze mirror, but as she stumbled backward, she bumped into something.

At the same moment, the footsteps stopped. Gao Ru Xue’s mind went blank. Acting on instinct alone, she slowly turned to look behind her.

A woman in corpse makeup and a wedding dress stood behind her, smiling.

“Ahh!” The piercing scream shattered the Haunted House’s silence; it could be heard even outside the building. Still tangled in the netting, Gao Ru Xue’s legs gave way and she collapsed to the floor.

All the fear she had been suppressing burst free as tears. Her eyes squeezed shut, and she struggled to steady her breathing.

“Xiao Wan, quickly bring her out!”

“Okay.” The female ghost standing in front of Gao Ru Xue removed the Bluetooth earpiece hidden beneath her hair and crouched down. “The experience ends here. Catch your breath. I’ll lead you out.”

Ten seconds later, the exit to the Minghun scenario opened. Chen Ge hurried over. “Only one? Where’s the other visitor?”

He had come running because he could no longer find He San on any of the surveillance feeds.

“That coward fainted after he ran into the room and saw the two mirrors. I was afraid he’d disrupt the next visitor’s experience, so I dragged him under the bed…”

“He fainted?” Even Chen Ge did not know how to respond. “Safety comes first. If this happens again, tell me immediately!”

“Yes, Boss.” Leaving Xu Wan to look after Gao Ru Xue, Chen Ge hurried into the room and pulled He San out from under the bed. The young man was completely unresponsive and looked badly shaken.

Sh*t, I need to get him outside into the fresh air.Chen Ge carried He San toward the Haunted House entrance, pulled back the heavy curtains, and kicked the gate open. “Please, give us some room!”

Chen Ge laid He San down near the entrance and tried to rouse him while asking the surrounding visitors to give them space. The sight stunned the people who had remained outside the attraction.

“Jesus Christ, what happened in there?”

“He visited the Haunted House and actually fainted? That’s a first.”

“He was scared unconscious, right? Then why do all the online reviews say this place isn’t scary?”

“F*ck, I’m starting to have chills…”

Not long afterward, Xu Wan emerged supporting Gao Ru Xue. The woman looked nothing like the composed visitor who had entered earlier. Her hair was disheveled, her face pale, and her steps unsteady; tear tracks still marked her cheeks.

“This is a completely different person!”

“What did she experience in there?”

“But why should they be afraid? Aren’t they forensic students?”

Xu Wan seated Gao Ru Xue on the steps and handed her a bottle of water. The woman was still recovering; the bottle trembled slightly in her hands.

“Don’t crowd them. Give them some air!” Chen Ge could feel a headache coming on. Gao Ru Xue had been frightened badly enough to cry, but what had happened to He San? Why had he suddenly fainted? If he was that easily scared, why hadn’t he just admitted it? Men and their pride…

The commotion drew more and more people toward the Haunted House. Eventually, it caught the attention of the park manager, who hurried over on his electric bike.

“Xiao Chen! What happened here? Why is there an unconscious visitor on the ground?!” Uncle Xu demanded as he jumped off his bike and pushed through the crowd.

“I’m not sure. Maybe it was the heat…” Even Chen Ge did not sound convinced.

“In this weather?” Uncle Xu hurried over to help He San onto his bike. “Whatever happened, we need to get him to the park clinic first!”

A few minutes later, He San finally began to stir. His eyelashes fluttered, and he slowly sat up on the bike. His eyes were unfocused, and he kept murmuring, “Mirror… mirror…”

“Easy, son. Stay calm!”

“Look, doesn’t he look possessed?”

After a few more minutes, He San seemed fully awake again. He scratched the back of his head and flushed with embarrassment when he realized the entire crowd was staring at him.

“Feeling better? Why did you faint in there?” Uncle Xu, still in his park uniform, handed He San a bottle of water.

“Honestly, I can’t remember exactly what happened. I got scared and ran through the first door I saw. There was a bronze mirror on the wall, and I remember someone calling my name, but everything after that is blank.” He San looked genuinely confused. “Was it some effect built into the Haunted House?”

“There’s a mirror-based scare inside the Haunted House?” Uncle Xu turned toward Chen Ge, whose expression had stiffened.
